background_art:
Effective task management and reminders play a
vital role in maintaining productivity and reducing stress.
Many individuals struggle with staying organized and effi-
ciently managing their tasks, often encountering issues such
as forgetting important deadlines, neglecting appointments,
and feeling overwhelmed due to a lack of structure. One
common challenge is relying solely on memory to recall
tasks, leading to forgetfulness and missed opportunities.
Lacking a centralized system for tracking tasks can result in
scattered information and overlooked items. Additionally,
various appointments and events are often scheduled in
different intervals (e.g., every three weeks vs. bi-weekly)
which can cause subsequent days or weeks to look different
and require different planning,
[0003] Another common challenge is keeping task man-
agement fun and interesting. Traditional task management
systems, such as calendars, lack the efficiency and enjoy-
ment brought by visual effects. Without these captivating
visual cues, the interface can become uninteresting and less
engaging, potentially resulting in reduced user interaction.
This absence of visual distinction can lead to information
overload, making it difficult for users to differentiate
between various events and tasks on their calendars, espe-
cially when they are scheduled at different intervals. More-
over, the lack of visual effects complicates the process of
prioritizing tasks and events, potentially causing users to
miss deadlines or forget appointments. The intuitiveness of
traditional task management applications suffers as users
may struggle to navigate and comprehend the interface
without visual cues, particularly affecting users with diverse
learning styles and accessibility requirements. Furthermore,
without visual effects, the emotional connection between
users and the traditional application weakens, as visual
effects often evoke emotions and create a more personalized
experience.

[0041] An object of the present disclosure is to help a user
stay organized by taking away the tedious work component
of setting up tasks, appointments, and tracking timelines (as
well as anticipate upcoming appointments) in traditional
task management applications, and instead, make managing
events more fun and engaging.
[0042] Another object of the present disclosure is to assist
users in tracking appointments and tasks related to their
body, while eliminating any negative connotations or need
for secrecy. The goal is to promote the idea that seeking
appointments for enhancing one’s appearance and well-
being is a normal and positive aspect of maintaining happiness and health.
[0043] Therefore, the disclosed embodiments relate to a
system and method for managing events using an avatar
based user interface. The disclosed system manages events
relating to a user’s body using a graphical user interface
(GUI). For instance, an avatar is used as a visual representation of the user’s body. The avatar may be configured to
any shape of the user’s body 1o help the user be comfortable with his/her/their appearance without any outside influence.
The user’s event information (e.g.. event data) is associated
with a body part of the avatar. A reminder is created for the
user based on the event information associated with the body
part of the avatar.

[0131] Additionally, the system 102 advantageously displays the message and selected body part simultaneously to help motivate the user. This dual presentation serves to further motivate the user, enhancing their engagement with the system 102. In other words, when a user receives a reminder, not only is the message clearly conveyed but also, in parallel, the relevant body part of the avatar is highlighted or represented. This visual connection between the reminder and the corresponding body part serves as a compelling visual cue, reinforcing the significance of the task or event associated with that particular body part. This approach contributes to a more immersive and effective user experience, strengthening the user’s commitment to fulfilling their responsibilities and appointments. It also makes the user’s particular avatar more familiar to the user’s unique experience (vs. a generic set of prescribed appointments for any user). For example, consider a user undergoing hormone therapy during their gender transition. In moments of doubt or discouragement, visualizing their preferred body or the appearance they aspire to achieve through the avatar can offer profound motivation and encouragement to persevere with the transitioning process.

[0132] The operation for system 102 may further include prompting the user to acknowledge the reminder (Block 314). Acknowledging the reminder means that the user takes some action to confirm that they have seen or recognized the reminder and are aware of the information or task it conveys. For example, the system 102 may remind the user of an event pertaining to a user’s hormone therapy. The notification may be displayed via the GUI 109 and include the therapy’s date, time, location, and any relevant information such as instructions or medication. In this case, for example, the user may be notified every day or week to take the necessary medication for hormone therapy. The user may then acknowledge the reminder by actuating an icon on the GUI 109 to dismiss the reminder, as depicted in FIG. 11.

The icon 1110 depicts a “DISMISS” button. The user may actuate (e.g., click or tap) the “DISMISS” button 1110 via the GUI 109.

[0134] FIG. 11 also illustrates a screenshot 1100, which includes an “Edit” icon. The icon 1112 depicts an “Edit” button. The user may actuate (e.g., click or tap) the “Edit” button 1112 via the GUI 109 to edit, update, and cancel existing events.

[0135] Acknowledging reminders offers several valuable advantages. By acknowledging a reminder, individuals can enhance their task management skills, ensuring that important events and responsibilities are not overlooked. Moreover, acknowledging reminders fosters a sense of accountability, motivating individuals to fulfill their commitments promptly. This interaction also drives user engagement with the application, leading to more personalized and efficient interactions. Ultimately, the practice of acknowledging reminders contributes to better organization, streamlined communication, and improved overall efficiency in daily activities.

[0136] Furthermore, the operation for system 102 may include assigning a priority level to the generated reminder based on a deadline of the reminder or a level of importance (Block 316). In other words, multiple reminders may be generated where each reminder is associated with a different and/or the same body part of the avatar. Each reminder may have a different deadline or level of importance.

[0137] One example of a criterion for determining the priority level of a reminder is its deadline. In other words, how soon a particular reminder needs to be acted upon or completed is a crucial factor. Reminders with closer deadlines are assigned higher priority levels, signifying that they require immediate attention or action. For example, the processor 103 determines a priority level based on the time before a deadline is reached. The closer a deadline approaches for an event, the higher the priority level is assigned to the event. A priority level may range from 0 to 5 with 5 being the highest or most urgent priority level.

[0138] The level of importance of a reminder is another example of a criterion of consideration for priority assignment. Not all reminders are of equal significance. Some tasks or events may be more critical than others. For example, a reminder for hormone therapy might be deemed more important than a reminder for a haircut appointment. The level of importance for each body part or event type is input by the user in the input section 802. The user may assign the level of importance in a range between 0 to 5 with 5 being the highest or most important. The above described criteria for determining a priority level of a reminder are examples and any number of other criteria may be used to determine a priority level.

[0139] To determine an overall priority level for a body part or event type associated with a body part, the processor 103 determines the average between the priority level assigned to a deadline and the priority level assigned to a level of importance. The overall priority level is then assigned to the corresponding body part and/or input event type. In another example, a separate priority level is assigned for each. In other words, a reminder for an event corresponding to a body part may be assigned one priority level based on corresponding deadlines alone and another priority level based on level of importance alone. In one example, the user may be able to select which priority level takes precedence. In another example, both priority levels remain associated with the reminder corresponding to the body part.

[0140] Thus, each reminder is assigned a priority level (or one or more priority levels) based on the deadline and/or level of importance. By assigning priority levels to these reminders, the system 102 can advantageously help users focus their attention on the most time-sensitive and critical matters.

[0141] The operation for system 102 may further include modifying the appearance of the at least one body part of the avatar associated with the reminder based on the assigned priority level (Block 318). In other words, the system 102 may provide visual cues for body parts of the avatar associated with a priority level for their reminders. Therefore, the system 102 has the capability to visually distinguish body parts of the avatar associated with different priority levels for their respective reminders. In this regard, the system 102 may create a “heat map,” which is a representation of data in the form of a map or diagram in which data values (priority levels in this example) are represented as colors, shades of black/grey/white, or other varying patterns and the like to distinguish values from one another.

[0142] FIG. 12 illustrates a screenshot 1200, which includes the avatar having body parts assigned to different priority levels, of a mobile device in accordance with an embodiment of the disclosed system. Referring to FIG. 12, the avatar 504 is depicted as having both its head and legs assigned a priority level. In this example, different colors or shadings are used to differentiate the different priority levels. Other indicators may be used, such as numerical call outs for each body part assigned a priority level, outlining the body parts, and the like. In other words, FIG. 12 illustrates a heat map where at least one body part, assigned a priority level, is represented by a distinct color or shade, effectively conveying the level of importance to the user. In one example, a darker color or shade may be indicative of a higher priority level.

[0143] For example, the system 102 receives event information concerning the user’s head and legs (or at least a portion of the legs). Subsequently, the system 102 associates the event information related to the user’s head with the avatar’s head and associates the event information concerning the user’s legs with the avatar’s legs. The event information concerning the user’s head is deemed to hold significant importance due to the context of a nose surgery, while the event information concerning the user’s legs holds lower importance, as it pertains to a waxing treatment. A first reminder based on the event information associated with the avatar’s head is generated, and a second reminder based on the event information tied to the avatar’s legs is generated. Consequently, the avatar’s head is granted a high-priority status in accordance with the level of importance, while the avatar’s legs are assigned a low-priority status. To visually convey this prioritization, alterations are made to the avatar’s appearance, as illustrated in FIG. 12. Specifically, the avatar’s head adopts a darker coloration to signal to the user that the reminder associated with the head carries a higher priority level than the reminder linked to the legs.

[0144] Another example may relate to multiple reminders being assigned priority levels based on their deadlines. For instance, when faced with multiple reminders scheduled for the same day, the system’s processor 103 compares the overall priority levels of each reminder, ensuring a streamlined display for the user. For instance, if a nose surgery reminder is designated a priority level of 5, surpassing a manicure reminder with a level 4 priority, the system employs a visual differentiation by displaying the reminders in different colors. This intuitive approach enables users to readily discern the varying urgency or importance of tasks. Furthermore, in cases where multiple reminders share the same highest priority level, the system maintains clarity by presenting them with a consistent pattern or color associated with that priority level, facilitating quick recognition of tasks of equal significance.

[0145] This dynamic prioritization ensures that urgent or time-critical tasks receive the user’s immediate attention, while tasks with more flexible timelines are acknowledged but do not disrupt the user’s focus on immediate, pressing matters.

[0146] In another example, when multiple reminders are linked to the same body part, a numerical badge may be shown next to or associated with the body part. This badge indicates the number of reminders or scheduled events associated with that specific body part. For example, if a separate event/reminder is associated with the eyes, nose, and mouth of the avatar, a numerical badge in the form of a small bubble, for example, may be displayed next to the head of the avatar with a number “3” to indicate that three events/reminders pertain to the head of the avatar. As described above, a user may select the head and zoom-in on the head to then either further select subparts of the head, such as the eyes, nose, or mouth, to see the different events/reminders associated with those body parts.

[0147] In another embodiment, the system 102 may employ various visual cues and alerts to communicate these priority levels effectively. High-priority reminders may trigger more noticeable alerts, such as popup notifications, vibrant colors, or sound cues, to capture the user’s attention promptly. In contrast, low-priority reminders may employ subtler visual indications, like muted colors or smaller notification icons, signaling their lower urgency without causing unnecessary distraction.

[0148] By adapting the avatar’s appearance and employing these intelligent priority assignments, the system 102 enhances the user’s experience by providing clear, context-aware cues that aid in managing and prioritizing tasks efficiently as it relates the avatar to the user’s own body. This ensures that the user remains in control of their schedule and can address their commitments effectively, whether they involve significant events like medical appointments or less critical tasks like personal grooming appointments.

[0149] The operation may also include storing a user’s personalized avatar under the user profile in the database 107. The user profile includes the personalized avatar having the generated reminders associated to at least one body part of the avatar. Storing the user’s avatar under the user’s profile preserves the avatar’s appearance, associated reminders, and also ensures that the user’s customization and preferences are readily accessible for future interactions.

[0150] Additionally, the operation may transmit or share the user’s profile to another user (Block 320), such as to enable collaboration between each user. By allowing the user to share their personalized avatar with other users, the system 102 advantageously allows users to coordinate and share events. Furthermore, users going through similar events may be able to come together to help each other through obstacles by sharing their avatars as an outline or template for guidance and inspiration. For example, a user’s avatar can serve as a source of inspiration, showing what is achievable and offering a clear path forward. Users can replicate successful approaches and adapt them to their own circumstances.

abstract: The following disclosure relates to a system and method for managing events using an avatar based user interface. The system includes: a graphical user interface (GUI) for a user to visually interact with an avatar; and at least one processor. The at least one processor is configured to: receive, via the GUI, event information pertaining to a body part of the user; associate the event information to a body part of the avatar, wherein the body part of the avatar corresponds to the body part of the user; and generate a reminder for the user based on the event information associated to the body part of the avatar.
